claims.text: The alloy is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy with interpenetrating or finely distributed phases.
The initial alloy surface is covered by an intact protective passive oxide film.
The protective oxide film is temperature-dependent.
The integrity of the protective oxide film at eutectic phase boundaries mediates coupled wear-corrosion degradation.
Mechanical wear removes or disrupts the oxide film at eutectic phase boundaries.
Wear prevents or limits reformation of the disrupted oxide film.
Oxide-film disruption exposes corrosion-susceptible microstructural constituents.
Exposure of vulnerable regions causes rapid localized corrosion at phase boundaries.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature produce an overall degradation rate greater than the sum of isolated wear and corrosion degradation rates.
The simultaneous condition increases material loss attributable to wear relative to isolated wear.
The simultaneous condition increases localized corrosion at exposed phase boundaries relative to isolated corrosion.
The magnitude of coupled degradation depends on alloy composition.
The magnitude of coupled degradation depends on oxide-film reformation kinetics.
The magnitude of coupled degradation depends on detailed microstructural features.

contradictions.description: The isolated tests are described as being conducted under the same load, sliding speed, and corrosive medium as the simultaneous test, while also being called solely wear or solely corrosion. A corrosion-only specimen cannot undergo the same sliding and load without introducing wear, and a wear-only specimen in the same active corrosive medium may still undergo corrosion unless corrosion is independently suppressed.
